steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Spray a shallow baking pan with cooking spray.

Sift both flours, 2 teaspoons sugar, salt, and baking soda together into a bowl. Cut in margarine until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Make a well in the center of the mixture and pour in 2 cups buttermilk and oil; stir with a spatula until dry mixture is completely moistened.

Transfer dough to a lightly floured surface and knead gently for no more than 1 minute. Place dough into the prepared pan; pat down and around to form a round loaf. Cut a cross in the top of the loaf with your finger. Brush the top with 1 tablespoon buttermilk, then sprinkle with 1 teaspoon sugar.

Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Reduce the heat to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C), then rotate the pan and bake for 30 more minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool on a wire rack before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Perfectly Moist Irish Wheaten Bread
raw_recipe.description: This Northern Irish-style wheaten bread recipe made with bread flour, whole wheat flour, buttermilk, sugar, and margarine makes a perfect loaf every time.

review.reviewBody:
Excellent recipe!
As a native Belfast man I can recommend this as perfect Wheaten bread.
Texture and consistency just right!
 
Didn't quite see the point of brushing with buttermilk or sprinkling with sugar prior to baking but it did no harm anyway.
 
There is absolutely no need to bake this within a pan and certainly this is something I have never heard of or come across before!
I formed the cake round onto a lightly floured Pizza baking stone.
Again, cutting the pre-baked bread with a finger is new to me and does not quite give the quartered effect achievable by knife.
Just make sure to cut no more than 1/3 to 1/2 way through to give the splendid quartering or 'flowering' effect desired on all wheaten or soda breads.

I used Olive Oil in lieu of vegetable and butter instead of margarine.

Buttermilk is not usually in one's pantry so you can add a small amount of vinegar or lemon juice to regular milk to substitute for buttermilk. Dry mix can be purchased.

The mixture stays easily on a pizza stone for baking.
This ensures the bread 'free-forms' as it should without using a spray buttered pan.

I have uploaded two photos.
Photo #7 shows the consistency of the pre-baked bread and #8 shows the finished product.
Serve with Irish smoked salmon.

UPDATE: 17th Mar 2011
I deleted some info to include this...
Reviewers have mentioned the bread as being "too crumbly".
Today I added 1 egg to the mixture and found it to be "tighter". See Photo #10 for the texture after egg addition.

Very very happy with the results. It came out perfect just like the submitter said it would. This bread has a wonderful hearty texture and natural nuttyness from the whole wheat. As suggested by another reviewer I used only 2 T. butter and 1/8 c. oil also only 1 tsp. salt and no sugar with outstanding results. It smelled amazing while it baked and tasted delicious after it cooled a bit and the next day toasted. This recipe is a winner! ** Update ** I have made this bread more times than any other recipe on this site. I have added varying combinations of seeds, nuts, and dried fruits (be creative) mix seeds, nuts, and/or dried fruits into the dry ingredients. This recipe is adaptable as long as you stay with the original amounts of flours, b. soda and buttermilk. This recipe deserves more than 5 stars!!

I had some left over buttermilk from a different recipe I wanted to use up and decided to try this recipe. It is fantastic!! I added 1 1/4 cup of raisins as well baked it in a loaf pan rather than a round pan and it turned out excellent!! I have made a few trips to the store specially to by buttermilk now for this recipe...it has not failed me yet!! It is a must try!!

Despite following the recipe to the letter the dough was more like a batter. I kept adding whole wheat and white flour in equal portions and salt and sugar (to balance flavor) until I could make it into a workable dough. 
I brushed it with some sour cream thinned with water (I had run out of buttermilk by that time) and followed cooking instructions exactly. It turned out great. 
My BF is from outside of Belfast and said this bread has the exact texture and taste his Auntie Mary used to make. 
If he says it tastes authentic then I’d definitely say it’s a win!!

This is a great alternative to soda bread! I made it for St. Paddy's day and changed the following: I used a buttermilk powder and water, brushed the crust with a salt water brine (water with a buch of salt), sprinkled a little red pepper and tarragon on the crust, and melted some butter over the top when it came out of the oven. Served with parsley butter (butter mixedith fresh parsley), corned beef, and a potato kugel. Mmmmm!

I liked this. At first bite, I wasn't sure what to think. I have never made an Irish bread. It sort of tasted like a beer bread, but then it wasn't quite sweet like one. It was more like a giant buttery and crunchy biscuit. I loved the crunchy outer coating and the inside was nice and soft. Later, I am going to try to cut each 1/4 or wedge into about 5 slices using my bread knife and guide. Unless one has a toaster oven, and could lay the slices flat, I am not sure how this would be toasted though. It might be easier after refrigerating. This is an extremely filling type bread. I will probably attempt it again, but more for something like St. Patrick Day. I found another recipe on here, basically the same, but fits in a 9x5 loaf pan for everyday. I flattened this to the size I wanted it for slicing, before baking. Note, though, it will puff up a little but it will widen to about double the size it went in the oven! Unlike some recipes I did follow this near exact with the good reviews. Only change was subbing salted butter for margarine, kneading directly in the bowl, and baking on parchment. It did take the full hour to bake.

Just got back from N. Ireland and wanted to match what I had every day there. This was reasonably close but a little too crumbly. Next time I'll add an egg as a previous reviewer suggested, and I'll increase the sugar by a tsp if not more. I love that this bread is yeast-free.

Best bread ever! When this came out off the oven, I ignored the part about waiting for it to cool down. The crust is crispy and thick and the inside is moist and delicious. The bread is crubly, and the bottom is very hard, but sooo good! I only used 2 Tbsp of butter, and after reducing the temperature baked for 20 minutes. It came out a perfect, golden brown.
*Update: I accidentally forgot the 3/4 c. whole wheat flour! I also put in slightly less than 1/4 c. oil, and still only 2 Tbsp. butter. However, the bread was still perfect and moist! I had to put it in a round cake pan because the dough was more like a batter. I did cook it for less time-about 40 min.

Superb recipe. I lived in Ireland for two years and this bread is even better than the package stuff you buy in Ireland. Although I made a couple adjustments. I didn't have buttermilk so I used regular milk and it turned out just fine and I added one egg to stiffen it up, so it's not so crumbly and you could spread butter on it. Other than that it came out perfect. Thank you for this wonderful recipe

Added an egg, just like Belfast Jimmy recommended and used butter (as my mom and nan would never have used margarine in a million years and, yep, they were Irish) ... It's a very moist mixture that you end up with before going into the oven, so don't add more flour ... my go to recipe for wheaten bread !

This is excellent and easy. Very moist and flavorful. I happened to have made bacon the same day, so I decided to be frugal and use bacon fat in place of the butter and the vegetable oil. I also made butter in my KA and used the buttermilk in the bread.

My partner is from Northern Ireland and we had been buying Wheaten bead when it was available in Marks & Spencers foodhall. Which was only occasionally as its obviously in high demand. I made this bread following the recipe diligently and wow! This tastes better than the one we were buying. He absolutely loved it, saying it tasted like home. Another loaf is currently in the oven. Thank you so much for this recipe.
I also ended up with a sloppy mess and by the time I had added huge amounts more of the flour, it was overworked and tough. The quantities are wrong.
Works great every time. Absolutely delicious, very easy and particularly suited to cold winter months with a bowl of soup or as a sandwich.
Absolutely delicious. I'm from Northern Ireland and this tastes better than the shop one.♡
This is my 2nd batch ,the first one was excellent so didn’t last long with grandchildren hence no 2 go . It’s lovely and moist and spongy , excellent toasted with cheese etc.

Being the first time ever at making soda bread, this is a very good bread. Somewhat sweet, nice nutty flavor. Nice crunchy crust, nice& moist center. Was easy to put together. Perfect recipe for anyones' first go at Soda bread.

I didn't change the recipe except for exchanging the wheat flour for white bread flour. I ended up with a gloppy mess, and had to add at least another 1/3 cup flour. It was still too sticky and it didn't bake well. It baked up heavy and undercooked on the inside - which could be my fault - but the knife came out clean when I checked the bread and it was a deep brown crust. Oh well...

My mother is from Northern Ireland. She didn't get to make her annual trip home this year because of the travel restrictions due to covid 19. This bread took her home! Just slap on some kerrygold butter, pour a cuppa tea, slice up some aged cheddar and enjoy along side a bowl of potato leek soup, yum! I added an egg and skipped the buttermilk and sugar on top, came out great, so easy & delicious!!!
I'm originally from N Ireland and its one of the best I've tasted. Will be making it again.
